solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One married type's impressions

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
print is type, and the 's reads as a plural S

explanation.surface: A married sort's impressions of something, as if describing a personality type.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprints are marks pressed into a surface, the same idea as impressions left behind.

clue.text: Manage to finish by thinking originally

indicators.note: by places the finishing word right beside the opening letter
originally points to the word's first letter, how thinking begins

parts.note: finish means end

explanation.surface: Someone managing to complete a task thanks to original thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend something is to look after it, as in manage a garden or a bar.

clue.text: Leant over and gave some helpful information

definitions.meaning: something leant over has been tilted to one side
to give someone a tip is to pass on useful advice

explanation.definitionFit: Tipped means both tilted and having given a useful pointer, two unrelated senses of one verb.

clue.text: In angry cry of pain start to brandish weapon

indicators.note: In tells us the next piece is placed inside the angry cry

parts.note: cross means angry
ow is an exclamation of pain

indicators.note: start to points to the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone yelling in pain and fury begins waving a weapon about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' wants to read as a link, but it signals that the brandish letter sits inside the angry cry of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a bow mounted on a stock, a medieval missile weapon.

clue.text: Blair's urge for transportation for such offences

indicators.note: transportation carries the letters to new places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's wish to have offenders shipped overseas, as in the old penal colonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for transportation' rearranges BLAIRSURGE. Transportation was the old British punishment of shipping convicts to Australia, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Burglaries are crimes of breaking in to steal, the kind of offences once punished by transportation.

clue.text: Sort of person that's below average

indicators.note: in a down answer, below puts this piece after the previous one

parts.note: the mean is the average
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A remark about someone who falls short of the norm.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is a stingy or unkind person, a particular type of individual.

clue.text: One forgets and means to change current account

indicators.note: to change tells us the word means must be rearranged

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A forgetful person who intends to alter their bank account.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesiac is someone suffering memory loss, one who forgets.

clue.text: Basket holding women's yarn

indicators.note: holding means the basket contains the next piece

parts.note: a creel is a wicker basket used by anglers
W abbreviates women, as on a lavatory door

explanation.surface: A basket in which the women keep their knitting wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewel is a fine worsted yarn used for embroidery.

clue.text: Soundly beaten by Germany on the way

indicators.note: on puts this piece on the end of the other in an across answer

parts.note: a route is the way to go
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A team thrashed by the Germans while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A routed army or side has been heavily defeated, put to flight.

clue.text: Without water, a journey is cut short

indicators.note: cut short tells us to remove the last letter of the journey word

parts.note: a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: A trip ends early because the travellers have run out of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land is dry, receiving little or no rainfall.

clue.text: Media representative gift wrapping flag

indicators.note: wrapping says the gift goes around the next piece

parts.note: a present is a gift
to flag is to tire or droop, to sag

explanation.surface: A publicist with a present done up in a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A press agent handles publicity for a client, dealing with the media on their behalf.

clue.text: Kept it in the family

parts.note: a playful description of breeding with close relatives rather than of keeping a secret

explanation.definitionFit: Something inbred results from mating between closely related relatives, keeping things within one family.

clue.text: Where to keep records of tie worn by caller

indicators.note: worn by places the tie inside the caller, as clothing is on its wearer

parts.note: a ringer is someone who rings, a caller
to bind is to tie

explanation.surface: A visitor wearing a necktie asks where the files are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring binder is a folder with metal rings for holding papers, a place to keep records.

clue.text: Two of them prepared to be adopted

indicators.note: Two of picks the final pair of letters from the word that follows

parts.note: braced means prepared for something

explanation.surface: A couple of children made ready to be taken in by a new family.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea or cause is to adopt it willingly.

clue.text: Makes an estimate selecting the most reasonable

indicators.note: selecting means a run of letters is chosen from within these words

explanation.surface: Someone who makes an estimate and picks the most sensible figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanest is the superlative of sane, meaning most sensible or reasonable.

clue.text: People over whom nurses go crazy

definitions.text: People over whom nurses go crazy

indicators.note: crazy shows the letters of the two words going wild into a new order

explanation.surface: The doctors that hospital nurses are said to swoon over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges NURSESGO; the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital romance tradition casts surgeons as the figures nurses fall for.

clue.text: Looking tired, heading off for cover

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: someone yawning looks tired

explanation.surface: A weary person setting off to find shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas sheet stretched out as shelter over a window or shopfront.

clue.text: My dog's nose is twitching

indicators.note: twitching makes the letters move about into a new order

parts.note: the words dog's supply the letters DOGS

explanation.surface: An owner remarks that their dog's nose keeps twitching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twitching' rearranges DOGSNOSE. 'My' is not a possessive here but an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: My and goodness are both mild exclamations of surprise, as in 'my goodness'.

clue.text: Impregnable cover protecting church silver for a period

indicators.note: protecting means the outer pair goes around the next pieces
cover means the outside letters of the word, which enclose the rest

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An unbreakable case guarding church silverware for a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' means the first and last letters of 'Impregnable', and 'protecting' wraps that pair round the church and silver.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice age is a long stretch of geological time when glaciers spread widely.

clue.text: Exclusion by pub one initially considers cruel

parts.note: a bar is an exclusion or ban
a bar is a pub
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A drinker thinks being banned by the pub is harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbaric means savagely cruel, uncivilised in its brutality.

clue.text: Stimulate a scheme to protect last of buffalo

indicators.note: to protect means the scheme goes around the next piece

parts.note: a ruse is a crafty scheme

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A plan to stir up interest in saving the bison.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse feelings is to stimulate or excite them.

clue.text: See boss start before I make purchases

indicators.note: start points to the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to shop is to make purchases

explanation.surface: Go and see the manager before I go shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not the verb but a diocese, so the head of a see is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop presides over a see, the diocese of which he is the head.

clue.text: Fool's position in form at school

definitions.meaning: Nick ... is the clownish weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
the lowest-ranked pupil in a class is at its foot

explanation.walkthrough: A form is a British school class.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comic weaver bears this name, and being last in class rankings also carries it.

clue.text: Take steps against token performance

parts.note: a counter is a token used in games
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: Fighting back against a merely symbolic show.
explanation.definitionFit: To counteract something is to act against it to neutralise its effect.

clue.text: Perfect condition for strike?

definitions.meaning: in ... condition means as new, flawless
to strike coins is to stamp them at a ...

explanation.definitionFit: Mint describes pristine condition and also, as a verb, stamping coins out of metal.

clue.text: Staff beginning to miss service

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: an ace in tennis is a serve the opponent cannot touch

explanation.surface: A player's opening miss on a serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a ceremonial staff carried as a symbol of authority.

clue.text: Bird following a second behind

indicators.note: following puts the bird after the other pieces

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird trailing just a moment behind another.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical word for at or towards the back of a ship, behind.

clue.text: Cause one to be dispirited?

parts.note: dispirited read literally as having spirits driven out rather than feeling low

explanation.definitionFit: To exorcise is to drive evil spirits out of a person or place.
